_**User (2026-04-21 01:04:20Z)**_

關於遠程clipboard sync (OSC52) 目前都有哪些settings?

> 然後另外我現在也有個痛點,就是我的neoVim的話,就是Yank的時候它會到system的clipboard,但是如果是remoteSSH的話,Yank的話就會相當於直接消失。就是沒有辦法跨Vim以外的應用使用。

```
有，這兩個痛點其實剛好是同一條線上的問題：remote SSH 裡的 Neovim yank 想回到你本機 clipboard，最穩的做法通常是走 OSC 52；而 tmux session 分享 本質上則是靠 tmux socket 權限 + SSH，不是 tmux 自己變成一個多人協作雲服務。 ￼

1. 為什麼本機 Nvim 可以進 system clipboard，但 SSH 上會「消失」？

因為本機 unnamedplus 常常是接到本機 clipboard provider；但你 SSH 到遠端之後，遠端 Nvim 不一定有能力直接操作你本機的 clipboard。Neovim 官方現在內建了 OSC 52 clipboard provider，而且明講：在 TUI 裡可以用 OSC 52 做 clipboard；但如果你在 tmux 之類的 terminal multiplexer 裡，自動偵測可能會失效，所以常常要手動強制開。另一个重點是：OSC 52 的 copy 通常可行，但 paste/read clipboard 不一定每個 terminal 都支援。 ￼

2. 你現在最推薦的解法

先把 Neovim 在 SSH 時強制走 OSC 52。

init.lua：

vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION then
  vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"
end

如果你想更明確一點，也可以不判斷 SSH，直接全域用：

vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"

這是 Neovim 官方文件直接支援的設定方式。 ￼

3. 但如果你有在 tmux 裡跑 Nvim，還要再補 tmux 設定

tmux 官方 wiki 說得很清楚：要讓 tmux 幫你把 copy 同步到外部 terminal clipboard，需要三件事同時成立：

1. set-clipboard 要是 on 或 external
2. Ms capability 要存在
3. 你的 terminal 本身要支援並啟用 OSC 52

而且 tmux wiki 還特別說：這條路最大的優點就是它能跨 SSH 工作，不需要 X11 forwarding。 ￼

你可以先這樣配 .tmux.conf：

set -s set-clipboard external

然後進 tmux 裡檢查：

tmux info | grep Ms:

如果看到 [missing]，tmux 官方 wiki 建議依照你 tmux 外面 的 $TERM 去補 terminal-overrides，例如：

set -as terminal-overrides ',xterm-256color:Ms=\E]52;%p1%s;%p2%s\007'

注意這個 xterm-256color 只是例子，你應該用你外部 terminal 真正的 $TERM。tmux 官方也提醒，改完 .tmux.conf 最好整個 tmux kill-server 後重開。 ￼

4. 一個很實際的排查順序

先照這順序測：

1. 不用 tmux，直接 SSH 進去跑 Nvim
    * 測試 "+yy
2. 再進 tmux 裡測一次
3. 在 tmux 裡跑：

tmux show -s set-clipboard
tmux info | grep Ms:

4. 確認你的本機 terminal 有沒有允許 OSC 52

如果「不用 tmux 可以、進 tmux 不行」，問題幾乎就是 tmux 那層。Neovim 官方也明講 multiplexer 會影響自動偵測；tmux 官方也明講 set-clipboard / Ms / terminal support` 三者都要到位。 ￼

5. 關於 tmux session 分享：是不是一定要同一個帳號？

不一定，但最簡單通常是同一個 Unix 帳號。
tmux man page 說，tmux server 預設建立的 socket 檔案權限會阻止除了 owner 和 root 以外的其他使用者存取；另外也有 server-access 可以調整某個使用者的 access 與 read/write 權限。不過官方同時警告：就算是 read-only，也不要隨便給不可信任的使用者。 ￼

也就是說：

* 同一帳號：最省事，兩個人都 SSH 成同一個 user，直接 tmux attach
* 不同帳號同一台機器：技術上可行，但要處理
    1. tmux socket 檔案系統權限
    2. tmux server-access 權限
        官方也提醒這件事要非常小心。 ￼

6. 有沒有只讀模式？

有。tmux 官方 man page 直接支援 read-only client。attach-session 的 -r 是 -f read-only,ignore-size 的別名；read-only client 只有 detach / switch-client 這類少數操作有效。 ￼

也就是說你可以這樣：

tmux attach -r -t mysession

這很適合「我想讓別人看，但不要亂按」。 ￼

7. 那 tmux 有沒有「加密機制」？

tmux 本身比較像是本機上的 terminal multiplexer server，安全模型主要是 Unix socket 權限控制；真正跨網路時，你通常是靠 SSH 連進同一台主機，所以傳輸加密主要來自 SSH，不是 tmux 額外做了一層多人共享加密協議。這點從 tmux man page 對 socket 權限、server-access、client attach 的設計就可以看出來。 ￼

8. 我對你的實戰建議

如果你現在最想解決的是 remote Nvim yank 回本機 clipboard：

先做這兩步就夠了。

init.lua：

vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"

.tmux.conf：

set -s set-clipboard external

然後檢查：

tmux info | grep Ms:
echo $TERM

如果 Ms 缺失，再補對應的 terminal-overrides。這通常就是最少改動、最接近「本機 Nvim 一樣好用」的方案。 ￼

如果你最想解決的是 tmux session 安全分享：

* 自己的小圈圈協作：同機器、同帳號最簡單
* 想給別人旁觀：tmux attach -r
* 不想共用帳號：才考慮 socket 權限 + server-access
* 不熟就不要直接開給不可信的其他 user，官方對這件事是有明確風險提醒的。 ￼

如果你願意，我下一則可以直接按你常見環境幫你出一份可貼上的設定：
Neovim + tmux + SSH + macOS 本機 terminal 的完整最小可用版。
```

```text
1	# tmux
2	
3	Managed tmux config lives under `~/.config/tmux/`, with a shim at `~/.tmux.conf` that sources the XDG entry point.
4	
5	## Source layout (in this repo)
6	
7	| Source | Deployed | Purpose |
8	|--------|----------|---------|
9	| [`dot_tmux.conf`](../../../dot_tmux.conf) | `~/.tmux.conf` | one-line shim |
10	| [`dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf) | `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` | entry point, picks theme |
11	| [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) | — | plugins + theme-agnostic options |
12	| [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) | — | all bind-keys and popup menu |
13	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | — | default theme (top status bar) |
14	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) | — | alternative theme (bottom status bar) |
15	| [`dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh`](../../../dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh) | `~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh` | responsive status bar for Catppuccin |
16	
17	This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:
18	
19	- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`
20	- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or tmux2k (bottom) — switchable at runtime
21	- Catppuccin status bar is responsive — modules adapt to terminal width (mobile-friendly)
22	- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
23	- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
24	- capture pane to clipboard helpers
25	- sesh integration for session picking
26	- `extended-keys` with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
27	- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled
28	- macOS terminal must send Option as Meta for `M-` bindings — see [ghostty.md](../ghostty.md)
29	
30	## In this folder
31	
32	- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu
33	- [themes.md](./themes.md) — Catppuccin / tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting
34	- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources
35	
36	## First-time setup
37	
38	After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.
39	
40	## Version requirement: tmux >= 3.3
41	
42	The popup menu at `prefix + Space` uses `display-menu -x R -y P`. On tmux 3.2a (shipped by Ubuntu 22.04 apt) the menu is positioned past the terminal's right edge and silently suppressed — the man page explicitly states _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ tmux 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`, so the menu renders correctly.
43	
44	The ansible `devtools` role now checks the tmux version and, when it is below 3.3, upgrades automatically:
45	
46	1. **Linuxbrew present** → `brew install tmux` (latest stable).
47	2. **No Linuxbrew, x86_64 Linux** → download [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage), extract to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root/` (no FUSE needed), and install a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux` that exec's the bundled binary. `~/.local/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin` in PATH so the newer binary wins.
48	3. **No Linuxbrew, non-x86_64** (e.g. armv7l, aarch64 servers without brew) → ansible prints a warning; build from source or enable Linuxbrew.
49	
50	### Switching a running server to the new binary
51	
52	After an upgrade, existing tmux servers keep running the old binary (a live process doesn't re-exec on PATH change). Clients attaching to the same socket also stay on the old version. To switch over:
53	
54	```bash
55	# lose current sessions but get a clean 3.3+ server
56	tmux kill-server
57	
58	# or: start the new server on a new socket and migrate sessions manually
59	tmux -L new new-session -s work
60	```
61	
62	Verify with `tmux -V` (binary version) and, inside tmux, `#{version}` in a format string (server version).
63	
64	## Reload Config
65	
66	Most changes do not need a server restart.
67	
68	```bash
69	tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
70	```
71	
72	Or, inside tmux: `prefix + R` (shows a confirmation message after reloading).
73	
74	If a change still behaves wrong, try a new pane/window first. Only `tmux kill-server` when a terminal-capability or plugin-init issue clearly survives a reload — e.g. switching themes without leftover styling.
75	
76	## Exit vs Detach
77	
78	- `prefix + d` — detach the current client, leaving the session running
79	- `exit` — close the current shell; when the last pane exits, the session ends
80	- `prefix + :` then `kill-session` — kill the current session immediately
81	- `tmux kill-server` — kill every session and stop the server
82	
83	`detach-on-destroy off` is set, so when you kill a session tmux switches to another one instead of detaching if other sessions exist.
84	
85	## Prefix Key
86	
87	Default: `Ctrl + b`. Examples in the sibling docs assume `prefix = Ctrl + b`.
88	
89	## Plugins
90	
91	| Plugin | Purpose |
92	|--------|---------|
93	| `tmux-resurrect` | Save/restore sessions across tmux restarts |
94	| `tmux-continuum` | Automatic session saving |
95	| `tmux-floax` | Floating scratch pane (`prefix+F` toggle, `prefix+P` menu) |
96	| `tmux-fzf-url` | `prefix+u` opens fzf popup with all URLs in pane |
97	| `tmux-open` | In copy-mode: `o` opens selection, `C-o` in editor, `S` search |
98	| `catppuccin/tmux` | Status bar theme (mocha, top bar) — default |
99	| `tmux2k` | Status bar theme (onedark, bottom bar) — alternative |
100	
101	Managed by TPM; `prefix + I` to install, `prefix + U` to update.
102	
103	## Verify current config
104	
105	```bash
106	ls ~/.config/tmux/
107	tmux display-message -p '#{@theme_variant}'
108	tmux list-keys -T prefix
109	tmux show-options -s | rg 'extended-keys|extended-keys-format|default-terminal'
110	tmux show-options -g | rg 'status|focus-events'
111	```
112

    "folke/snacks.nvim",
    opts = function(_, opts)
      -- The util.project extra inserts into preset.keys with key="P" and
      -- desc="Projects (util.project)". Fix to lowercase "p" and clean label.
      local keys = vim.tbl_get(opts, "dashboard", "preset", "keys")

-- https://www.reddit.com/r/neovim/comments/156c9nh/how_to_use_tab_to_confirm_first_autocomplete_in/
-- https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/discussions/39#discussioncomment-6069716
-- https://www.lazyvim.org/configuration/recipes
-- https://www.reddit.com/r/neovim/comments/19054s4/help_how_do_i_auto_complete_with_tab_in_lazyvim/
-- https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/wiki/Example-mappings#intellij-like-mapping
-- https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/discussions/250
return {
  {
    "L3MON4D3/LuaSnip",
    keys = function()
      return {}
    end,
  },
  {
    "hrsh7th/nvim-cmp",
    dependencies = {
      "hrsh7th/cmp-emoji",
    },
    ---@param opts cmp.ConfigSchema
    opts = function(_, opts)
      local cmp = require("cmp")

      opts.mapping = vim.tbl_extend("force", opts.mapping, {
        ["<Tab>"] = cmp.mapping(function(fallback)
          -- This little snippet will confirm with tab, and if no entry is selected, will confirm the first item
          if cmp.visible() then
            local entry = cmp.get_selected_entry()
            if not entry then
              cmp.select_next_item({ behavior = cmp.SelectBehavior.Select })
            else
              cmp.confirm()
            end
          else
            fallback()
          end
        end, { "i", "s" }),
      })
    end,
  },
}

  opts = {
    numhl = true,
    sign_priority = 15, -- higher than diagnostic,todo signs. lower than dapui breakpoint sign
    on_attach = function(bufnr)
      local gs = package.loaded.gitsigns

      local function map(mode, lhs, rhs, desc)
        vim.keymap.set(mode, lhs, rhs, { buffer = bufnr, desc = desc })
      end

      map("n", "]h", gs.next_hunk, "Next Git hunk")
      map("n", "[h", gs.prev_hunk, "Prev Git hunk")

      map("n", "<leader>hp", gs.preview_hunk, "Preview hunk")
      map("n", "<leader>hP", gs.preview_hunk_inline, "Preview hunk inline")

      map("n", "<leader>hs", gs.stage_hunk, "Stage hunk")
      map("n", "<leader>hr", gs.reset_hunk, "Revert hunk")

      map("v", "<leader>hs", function()
        gs.stage_hunk({ vim.fn.line("."), vim.fn.line("v") })
      end, "Stage selection")
      map("v", "<leader>hr", function()
        gs.reset_hunk({ vim.fn.line("."), vim.fn.line("v") })
      end, "Revert selection")

      map("n", "<leader>hd", gs.toggle_deleted, "Toggle deleted (inline)")
    end,
  },
}

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 2026-04-21 01:04:58Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="Read"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./.specstory/history/2026-04-21_01-03-47Z-clipboard-sync-osc52-settings.md`

```text
1	<!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 -->
2	
3	# 2026-04-21 01:04:20Z
4	
5	<!-- Claude Code Session 0214acc4-8f39-4075-9177-b6bbfa07f0f6 (2026-04-21 01:04:20Z) -->
6	
7	_**User (2026-04-21 01:04:20Z)**_
8	
9	關於遠程clipboard sync (OSC52) 目前都有哪些settings?
10	
11	> 然後另外我現在也有個痛點,就是我的neoVim的話,就是Yank的時候它會到system的clipboard,但是如果是remoteSSH的話,Yank的話就會相當於直接消失。就是沒有辦法跨Vim以外的應用使用。
12	
13	```
14	有，這兩個痛點其實剛好是同一條線上的問題：remote SSH 裡的 Neovim yank 想回到你本機 clipboard，最穩的做法通常是走 OSC 52；而 tmux session 分享 本質上則是靠 tmux socket 權限 + SSH，不是 tmux 自己變成一個多人協作雲服務。 ￼
15	
16	1. 為什麼本機 Nvim 可以進 system clipboard，但 SSH 上會「消失」？
17	
18	因為本機 unnamedplus 常常是接到本機 clipboard provider；但你 SSH 到遠端之後，遠端 Nvim 不一定有能力直接操作你本機的 clipboard。Neovim 官方現在內建了 OSC 52 clipboard provider，而且明講：在 TUI 裡可以用 OSC 52 做 clipboard；但如果你在 tmux 之類的 terminal multiplexer 裡，自動偵測可能會失效，所以常常要手動強制開。另一个重點是：OSC 52 的 copy 通常可行，但 paste/read clipboard 不一定每個 terminal 都支援。 ￼
19	
20	2. 你現在最推薦的解法
21	
22	先把 Neovim 在 SSH 時強制走 OSC 52。
23	
24	init.lua：
25	
26	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
27	if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION then
28	  vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"
29	end
30	
31	如果你想更明確一點，也可以不判斷 SSH，直接全域用：
32	
33	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
34	vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"
35	
36	這是 Neovim 官方文件直接支援的設定方式。 ￼
37	
38	3. 但如果你有在 tmux 裡跑 Nvim，還要再補 tmux 設定
39	
40	tmux 官方 wiki 說得很清楚：要讓 tmux 幫你把 copy 同步到外部 terminal clipboard，需要三件事同時成立：
41	
42	1. set-clipboard 要是 on 或 external
43	2. Ms capability 要存在
44	3. 你的 terminal 本身要支援並啟用 OSC 52
45	
46	而且 tmux wiki 還特別說：這條路最大的優點就是它能跨 SSH 工作，不需要 X11 forwarding。 ￼
47	
48	你可以先這樣配 .tmux.conf：
49	
50	set -s set-clipboard external
51	
52	然後進 tmux 裡檢查：
53	
54	tmux info | grep Ms:
55	
56	如果看到 [missing]，tmux 官方 wiki 建議依照你 tmux 外面 的 $TERM 去補 terminal-overrides，例如：
57	
58	set -as terminal-overrides ',xterm-256color:Ms=\E]52;%p1%s;%p2%s\007'
59	
60	注意這個 xterm-256color 只是例子，你應該用你外部 terminal 真正的 $TERM。tmux 官方也提醒，改完 .tmux.conf 最好整個 tmux kill-server 後重開。 ￼
61	
62	4. 一個很實際的排查順序
63	
64	先照這順序測：
65	
66	1. 不用 tmux，直接 SSH 進去跑 Nvim
67	    * 測試 "+yy
68	2. 再進 tmux 裡測一次
69	3. 在 tmux 裡跑：
70	
71	tmux show -s set-clipboard
72	tmux info | grep Ms:
73	
74	4. 確認你的本機 terminal 有沒有允許 OSC 52
75	
76	如果「不用 tmux 可以、進 tmux 不行」，問題幾乎就是 tmux 那層。Neovim 官方也明講 multiplexer 會影響自動偵測；tmux 官方也明講 set-clipboard / Ms / terminal support` 三者都要到位。 ￼
77	
78	5. 關於 tmux session 分享：是不是一定要同一個帳號？
79	
80	不一定，但最簡單通常是同一個 Unix 帳號。
81	tmux man page 說，tmux server 預設建立的 socket 檔案權限會阻止除了 owner 和 root 以外的其他使用者存取；另外也有 server-access 可以調整某個使用者的 access 與 read/write 權限。不過官方同時警告：就算是 read-only，也不要隨便給不可信任的使用者。 ￼
82	
83	也就是說：
84	
85	* 同一帳號：最省事，兩個人都 SSH 成同一個 user，直接 tmux attach
86	* 不同帳號同一台機器：技術上可行，但要處理
87	    1. tmux socket 檔案系統權限
88	    2. tmux server-access 權限
89	        官方也提醒這件事要非常小心。 ￼
90	
91	6. 有沒有只讀模式？
92	
93	有。tmux 官方 man page 直接支援 read-only client。attach-session 的 -r 是 -f read-only,ignore-size 的別名；read-only client 只有 detach / switch-client 這類少數操作有效。 ￼
94	
95	也就是說你可以這樣：
96	
97	tmux attach -r -t mysession
98	
99	這很適合「我想讓別人看，但不要亂按」。 ￼
100	
101	7. 那 tmux 有沒有「加密機制」？
102	
103	tmux 本身比較像是本機上的 terminal multiplexer server，安全模型主要是 Unix socket 權限控制；真正跨網路時，你通常是靠 SSH 連進同一台主機，所以傳輸加密主要來自 SSH，不是 tmux 額外做了一層多人共享加密協議。這點從 tmux man page 對 socket 權限、server-access、client attach 的設計就可以看出來。 ￼
104	
105	8. 我對你的實戰建議
106	
107	如果你現在最想解決的是 remote Nvim yank 回本機 clipboard：
108	
109	先做這兩步就夠了。
110	
111	init.lua：
112	
113	vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
114	vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"
115	
116	.tmux.conf：
117	
118	set -s set-clipboard external
119	
120	然後檢查：
121	
122	tmux info | grep Ms:
123	echo $TERM
124	
125	如果 Ms 缺失，再補對應的 terminal-overrides。這通常就是最少改動、最接近「本機 Nvim 一樣好用」的方案。 ￼
126	
127	如果你最想解決的是 tmux session 安全分享：
128	
129	* 自己的小圈圈協作：同機器、同帳號最簡單
130	* 想給別人旁觀：tmux attach -r
131	* 不想共用帳號：才考慮 socket 權限 + server-access
132	* 不熟就不要直接開給不可信的其他 user，官方對這件事是有明確風險提醒的。 ￼
133	
134	如果你願意，我下一則可以直接按你常見環境幫你出一份可貼上的設定：
135	Neovim + tmux + SSH + macOS 本機 terminal 的完整最小可用版。
136	```

```text
1	# tmux — Keybindings
2	
3	All bindings use the default prefix `Ctrl + b`.
4	
5	## Daily Workflow
6	
7	| Keybinding | Action |
8	|------------|--------|
9	| `prefix + R` | Reload `~/.tmux.conf` |
10	| `prefix + Space` | Open the tmux popup menu |
11	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh picker |
12	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh picker via television (tv) |
13	| `prefix + O` | Open sesh built-in picker |
14	| `prefix + W` | Open sesh window picker (fzf) |
15	| `prefix + S` | Jump to the last sesh session |
16	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to the git root session for the current repo |
17	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
18	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
19	| `prefix + M` | Move current window to another session (prompts for `session[:index]`) |
20	| `prefix + B` | Break current pane into a new window and move it to a session (tab tear-out) |
21	| `prefix + A` | Link current window into another session (window appears in both) |
22	| `prefix + d` | Detach |
23	| `prefix + t` | Show tmux clock mode |
24	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
25	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
26	
27	## Panes and Windows
28	
29	| Keybinding | Action |
30	|------------|--------|
31	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (requires CSI-u terminal: Ghostty, Alacritty, Kitty) |
32	| `Ctrl + 0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (same as `prefix + 9`) |
33	| `Ctrl + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes — crosses into Neovim splits (vim-tmux-navigator) |
34	| `Ctrl + \` | Focus previous pane/split (vim-tmux-navigator) |
35	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Move between panes (fallback, tmux-only) |
36	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells, repeatable) |
37	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell, repeatable) |
38	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
39	| `prefix + \|` | Split left/right (vertical divider) |
40	| `prefix + -` | Split top/bottom (horizontal divider) |
41	| `prefix + c` | New window in current path |
42	| `prefix + x` | Kill pane |
43	| `prefix + z` | Toggle pane zoom |
44	| `prefix + {` | Swap pane with previous (left/up) |
45	| `prefix + }` | Swap pane with next (right/down) |
46	| `prefix + [` | Enter copy mode |
47	
48	`Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support. Ghostty/cmux sends these natively. Alacritty needs explicit `keyboard.bindings` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`). Legacy terminals (Terminal.app, plain SSH) cannot send these — use `prefix + number` instead.
49	
50	Swap-pane swaps the **content** while keeping the **sizes**. So if you have a 75%/25% split and swap, the left pane's content moves to the right (25%) and vice versa — the proportions stay fixed.
51	
52	## Layouts
53	
54	| Keybinding | Action |
55	|------------|--------|
56	| `M-1` | Even horizontal layout |
57	| `M-2` | Even vertical layout |
58	| `M-3` | Main horizontal layout |
59	| `M-4` | Main vertical layout |
60	| `M-5` | Tiled layout |
61	| `prefix + E` | Spread panes evenly (built-in) |
62	
63	`M-1` through `M-5` are tmux built-ins — no prefix needed; just hold Meta (Alt/Option) and press the number.
64	
65	> **macOS terminal requirement**: Option must send Meta/Esc+ for `M-` bindings to work. Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed by this repo in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). Alacritty: `window.option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. iTerm2: Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](../ghostty.md).
66	
67	## Floating Pane (tmux-floax)
68	
69	| Keybinding | Action |
70	|------------|--------|
71	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (80% width/height) |
72	| `prefix + P` | Open floax popup menu |
73	
74	The floating pane uses a dedicated tmux session named `float` (hidden from sesh picker via blacklist). It inherits the current pane path. Useful for quick terminal tasks without disrupting your layout.
75	
76	## Copy Mode (Vim-Style)
77	
78	Enter with `prefix + [`. Navigate with vim keys, then:
79	
80	| Key | Action |
81	|-----|--------|
82	| `v` | Begin character selection (visual mode) |
83	| `V` | Select entire line |
84	| `C-v` | Toggle rectangle/block selection |
85	| `y` | Yank selection to system clipboard |
86	| `/` | Search forward |
87	| `?` | Search backward |
88	| `n`/`N` | Next/previous search match |
89	| `g`/`G` | Jump to top/bottom |
90	| `C-u`/`C-d` | Half-page up/down |
91	| `q` or `Escape` | Exit copy mode |
92	
93	Mouse drag in copy mode also copies to clipboard. Double-click selects a word.
94	
95	## Right-click menus
96	
97	Right-click opens a context menu depending on where you click:
98	
99	| Target | Menu |
100	|--------|------|
```

 `./docs/tools/ghostty.md`

```text
1	# Ghostty & cmux
2	
3	[Ghostty](https://ghostty.org/) is a fast, native terminal emulator. [cmux](https://cmux.dev/) is a lightweight macOS terminal built on Ghostty for managing AI coding agents. Both read the same config file.
4	
5	## Managed config
6	
7	This repo manages `~/.config/ghostty/config` (via `dot_config/ghostty/config`). cmux reads this file first (before `~/Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config`).
8	
9	Key settings:
10	
11	- **`macos-option-as-alt = left`** — Left Option sends Meta/Esc+ so tmux `M-` keybindings work (theme switching `M-c`/`M-t`, layouts `M-1`..`M-5`, fine resize `M-h/j/k/l`). Right Option retains macOS compose behavior for accents and special characters.
12	- **`font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig`** — Disables ligatures for code readability.
13	
14	> **Note**: Restart Ghostty/cmux after changing the config — it is read on launch, not hot-reloaded.
15	
16	Without `macos-option-as-alt`, macOS Option produces Unicode compose characters (e.g. `Option+c` → `ç`) instead of `Esc+c`, silently breaking all tmux Meta bindings. Alacritty and iTerm2 have their own equivalent settings (`window.option_as_alt` and Profiles > Keys > Left Option Key > Esc+ respectively).
17	
18	## `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on remote hosts
19	
20	When you SSH into a fresh remote, `$TERM=xterm-ghostty` but the remote has no matching terminfo entry. Symptoms: broken line-drawing, garbled prompts, `clear`/`tput` failures, Neovim rendering glitches. This is especially visible on the first cmux/tmux SSH into a new box.
21	
22	### Option 1 — Ghostty built-in (recommended for interactive shells)
23	
24	> - [Shell Integration - Features](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration#ssh-integration)
25	
26	Add to `~/.config/ghostty/config`:
27	
28	```ini
29	shell-integration-features = ssh-env,ssh-terminfo
30	```
31	
32	- `ssh-terminfo`: auto-installs `xterm-ghostty` on the remote the first time you `ssh` from an interactive shell with Ghostty shell integration loaded.
33	- `ssh-env`: forwards `COLORTERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` via `SendEnv`, and falls back to `TERM=xterm-256color` where needed. The remote `sshd_config` needs a matching `AcceptEnv` line for the forwarded vars to take effect.
34	
35	**Limitations**: only triggers from interactive shells with the Ghostty wrapper active. It does not cover `ssh` invoked inside tmux/cmux panes, from scripts, or from wrapper tools (`rsync`, `aws`, `gcloud`, …). For those, use the manual helper below.
36	
37	### Option 2 — manual helper (works everywhere)
38	
39	A zsh function `ghostty-ssh-terminfo` is defined in [`dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`](../../dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh).
40	
41	```bash
42	ghostty-ssh-terminfo <ssh-host>
43	```
44	
45	What it does:
46	
47	- Validates local `infocmp` and the `xterm-ghostty` entry exist.
48	- Pipes `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` into a **single** SSH call (no double password/MFA prompt).
49	- On the remote: probes for `tic`, creates `~/.terminfo`, and runs `TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -` — so no root/sudo needed.
50	- Suppresses only the harmless `older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias` warning (emitted by ncurses < 6.3). Real errors still surface and set a non-zero exit.
51	
52	Example:
53	
54	```bash
55	# First time connecting a new box from cmux/tmux
56	ghostty-ssh-terminfo remote
57	# → Installed xterm-ghostty terminfo on remote (in ~/.terminfo)
58	
59	# Verify
60	ssh remote 'infocmp xterm-ghostty >/dev/null && echo ok'
61	```
62	
63	### Smoke-test against `localhost`
64	
65	Yes — if `sshd` is running locally you can validate the function without touching a real remote:
66	
67	```bash
68	# Enable sshd (Linux)
69	sudo systemctl start ssh
70	# or macOS: System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login
71	
72	ghostty-ssh-terminfo localhost
73	```
74	
75	Caveats:
76	
77	- `localhost` already has your own `$HOME`, so this effectively writes to the *same* `~/.terminfo` your local shell reads. Useful as a wiring/error-path smoke test, not as a representative "fresh remote" check.
78	- If you already have the entry locally (which you do, otherwise `infocmp -x xterm-ghostty` would fail), the install is a no-op overwrite — still exercises the full pipeline end-to-end.
79	- For a cleaner test, point at a container or a VM where `xterm-ghostty` is definitely missing.
80	
81	## Why the warning appears (and can't be fully fixed client-side)
82	
83	The `|`-separated long description in Ghostty's terminfo is interpreted as an extra alias by `tic` / ncurses prior to 6.3. The entry still installs correctly; the warning is cosmetic. The only real fix is upgrading ncurses on the remote.
84	
85	## See also
86	
87	- [tmux](tmux.md) — tmux config and keybindings (cmux runs on top of tmux).
88	- [sesh](../sesh.md) — session picker used in the tmux setup.
89
```
</details></tool-use>

# OSC 52 Clipboard Sync — Optimization Plan

## Context

The user wants remote-SSH Neovim `yank` to land in the **local (client) machine's** system clipboard, so copied text can be pasted into other apps outside Vim. Current repo state:

| Layer | Status |
|-------|--------|
| tmux (`dot_config/tmux/common.conf:79,82`) | ✅ `set -g set-clipboard on`, `set -g allow-passthrough on` |
| tmux `terminal-features` | ⚠️ Only `RGB` + `extkeys` declared — no explicit `clipboard` feature |
| Ghostty (`dot_config/ghostty/config`) | ⚠️ Relies on defaults (`clipboard-write = allow`, `clipboard-read = ask`) |
| Alacritty (`dot_config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`) | ✅ Native OSC 52 support, no special config needed |
| **Neovim** (`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`) | ❌ **Empty** — no `clipboard` / `g.clipboard` set; LazyVim defaults to local `pbcopy`/`xclip` which break over SSH |
| zsh | No clipboard hooks (not needed) |

**Root cause of the pain point**: the tmux side is already correct, but Neovim itself never routes its `+` register through OSC 52 when running on a remote host. Over SSH, the default provider tries to call `pbcopy`/`xclip` on the **remote** box, so yanks vanish from the local clipboard's perspective.

**Minor correction to the external advice pasted by the user**:
- `vim.g.clipboard = "osc52"` (string form) is **not** a stable Neovim API. The canonical form is the explicit table using `require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")` — supported since Neovim 0.10, matches the repo's `>= 0.11.2` requirement.
- `set -s set-clipboard external` is wrong scope: `set-clipboard` is a session option (`-g`), not a server option (`-s`). Current `set -g set-clipboard on` is already fine — no change needed there.
- In tmux 3.2+, the clean way to signal OSC 52 support is `terminal-features …:clipboard`, not an `Ms=` `terminal-overrides` override.

**Intended outcome**: yank inside remote Neovim (with or without tmux) puts text into the local macOS/Linux clipboard, pasteable into any app.

---

## Changes

### 1. Neovim — add OSC 52 clipboard provider (primary fix)

**File**: `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`

Replace the empty file body with:

\```lua
-- Options are automatically loaded before lazy.nvim startup
-- Default options: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/main/lua/lazyvim/config/options.lua

-- System clipboard integration
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"

-- Over SSH, route the + and * registers through OSC 52 so yanks reach
-- the LOCAL terminal's clipboard (pbcopy/xclip on the remote are useless here).
-- Locally (no SSH), keep LazyVim's default provider (pbcopy on macOS, etc.)
-- which also supports paste.
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end
\```

**Why SSH-conditional instead of always-on**: OSC 52 *paste* is poorly supported by many terminals (Ghostty prompts, Alacritty doesn't read at all). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves normal paste behaviour; forcing OSC 52 only when needed.

### 2. tmux — declare the `clipboard` terminal feature (defensive)

**File**: `dot_config/tmux/common.conf` (near line 70, next to the existing `terminal-features`)

Add one line after line 70:

\```tmux
set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
\```

**Why**: tmux 3.2+ enables OSC 52 only if it believes the outer terminal supports it. For most modern terminals it auto-detects, but explicit declarations make the behaviour independent of the shipped terminfo on a given host. `set -g set-clipboard on` on line 79 stays as-is.

### 3. Ghostty — pin the clipboard policy explicitly (optional but recommended)

**File**: `dot_config/ghostty/config`

Append:

\```conf
# OSC 52 clipboard policy
# - write: allow inner apps (Neovim via OSC 52) to set the system clipboard
# - read: keep the default "ask" (safer — apps can't silently exfiltrate)
clipboard-write = allow
clipboard-read = ask
\```

Both values match current defaults, but making them explicit prevents surprises if Ghostty upstream changes defaults, and serves as self-documentation.

### 4. Documentation updates

- **`docs/tools/tmux/README.md`** — extend the existing "OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled" note with a short troubleshooting sub-section: how to verify with `tmux info | grep -E 'Ms|clipboard'`, and reminder that `tmux kill-server` is needed for config changes to a running server.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** → Tmux Configuration → "Key Settings for Coding Agents" — extend the `set-clipboard on` line to mention the Neovim-side pairing.
- **`README.md`** — under "What You Get > Config Files", add a one-liner mentioning OSC 52 remote-clipboard behaviour (per the repo rule about keeping README.md in sync).

### 5. (Deferred — not doing now)

`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` has `prefix + y / Y / C-y` that call `pbcopy/xclip/xsel` directly (lines 79–110). These also break over SSH (they shell out on the remote host). A cleaner fix would be to route them through `load-buffer -b … ; paste-buffer` relying on `set-clipboard on` to emit OSC 52. **Not in scope for this plan** — the user's explicit pain point is Neovim yank, and changing those bindings risks regressing local behaviour. Flagged here for a possible follow-up.

---

## Critical files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` | **Primary** — add `unnamedplus` + SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard` |
| `dot_config/tmux/common.conf` | Add `terminal-features :clipboard` for common terminals |
| `dot_config/ghostty/config` | Pin `clipboard-write`/`clipboard-read` explicitly |
| `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` | Troubleshooting sub-section |
| `CLAUDE.md` | One-line note under tmux Key Settings |
| `README.md` | One-liner under Config Files |

No new plugins, no new ansible roles, no chezmoi templates touched.

---

## Verification

After `chezmoi apply`, on **local macOS** first (baseline):

1. `nvim /tmp/test.txt` → type a line → `yy` → switch to another app (browser) → `Cmd+V` → should paste. Confirms local provider still works (outside SSH, we did not change anything).

Then, on a **remote Linux box over SSH** (reproduces the user's pain point):

2. **Without tmux**: `ssh remote-box`, `nvim /tmp/x`, type + `yy`, then `Cmd+V` into a local macOS app → should paste.
3. **With tmux on the remote**: `ssh remote-box -t tmux new -A`, `nvim /tmp/x`, type + `yy`, `Cmd+V` locally → should paste.
4. Run on the remote:

   \```bash
   tmux info | grep -Ei 'ms|clipboard'
   echo "$TERM"
   \```

   Expect a `clipboard: true` / `Ms: \E]52;...` entry (not `[missing]`).
5. `:checkhealth provider.clipboard` inside Neovim on the remote — expect it to report the OSC 52 provider as active.

**Regression checks**:

- Local Neovim paste (`"+p`) should still work (we only override `g.clipboard` when `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` is set).
- tmux copy-mode `y` → still copies to local clipboard (already worked; no change there).

---

## Non-goals

- No change to `set-clipboard` value (stays `on`).
- No new OSC 52 plugin (`ojroques/nvim-osc52`) — Neovim's builtin `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` covers it.
- No tmux session-sharing / read-only-attach work (discussed in the pasted conversation but orthogonal to the yank problem).
- No changes to `prefix + y / Y / C-y` pane-capture bindings (deferred, see §5).

1	# tmux
2	
3	Managed tmux config lives under `~/.config/tmux/`, with a shim at `~/.tmux.conf` that sources the XDG entry point.
4	
5	## Source layout (in this repo)
6	
7	| Source | Deployed | Purpose |
8	|--------|----------|---------|
9	| [`dot_tmux.conf`](../../../dot_tmux.conf) | `~/.tmux.conf` | one-line shim |
10	| [`dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf) | `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` | entry point, picks theme |
11	| [`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf) | — | plugins + theme-agnostic options |
12	| [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) | — | all bind-keys and popup menu |
13	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf) | — | default theme (top status bar) |
14	| [`dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf`](../../../dot_config/tmux/theme.tmux2k.conf) | — | alternative theme (bottom status bar) |
15	| [`dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh`](../../../dot_config/tmux/executable_responsive.sh) | `~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh` | responsive status bar for Catppuccin |
16	
17	This setup is tuned for coding-agent and Neovim workflows:
18	
19	- native popup menu on `prefix + Space`
20	- Catppuccin (default, top status bar) or tmux2k (bottom) — switchable at runtime
21	- Catppuccin status bar is responsive — modules adapt to terminal width (mobile-friendly)
22	- vim-style pane navigation and copy mode
23	- URL opening via fzf (`prefix + u`) and tmux-open in copy mode
24	- capture pane to clipboard helpers
25	- sesh integration for session picking
26	- `extended-keys` with `csi-u` so keys like `Ctrl+/` reach Neovim inside tmux
27	- OSC 52 clipboard and OSC passthrough enabled
28	- macOS terminal must send Option as Meta for `M-` bindings — see [ghostty.md](../ghostty.md)
29	
30	## In this folder
31	
32	- [keybindings.md](./keybindings.md) — all keybindings and the popup menu
33	- [themes.md](./themes.md) — Catppuccin / tmux2k selection, switching, troubleshooting
34	- [vim.md](./vim.md) — tmux × Vim/Neovim notes and external resources
35	
36	## First-time setup
37	
38	After `chezmoi apply`, start tmux and run `prefix + I` once to let TPM install the plugins. The theme files also auto-clone their plugin on first source as a safety net, but TPM is the canonical installer.
39	
40	## Version requirement: tmux >= 3.3
41	
42	The popup menu at `prefix + Space` uses `display-menu -x R -y P`. On tmux 3.2a (shipped by Ubuntu 22.04 apt) the menu is positioned past the terminal's right edge and silently suppressed — the man page explicitly states _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ tmux 3.3 introduced position clamping and arithmetic in `-x`/`-y`, so the menu renders correctly.
43	
44	The ansible `devtools` role now checks the tmux version and, when it is below 3.3, upgrades automatically:
45	
46	1. **Linuxbrew present** → `brew install tmux` (latest stable).
47	2. **No Linuxbrew, x86_64 Linux** → download [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage), extract to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root/` (no FUSE needed), and install a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux` that exec's the bundled binary. `~/.local/bin` sits ahead of `/usr/bin` in PATH so the newer binary wins.
48	3. **No Linuxbrew, non-x86_64** (e.g. armv7l, aarch64 servers without brew) → ansible prints a warning; build from source or enable Linuxbrew.
49	
50	### Switching a running server to the new binary
51	
52	After an upgrade, existing tmux servers keep running the old binary (a live process doesn't re-exec on PATH change). Clients attaching to the same socket also stay on the old version. To switch over:
53	
54	```bash
55	# lose current sessions but get a clean 3.3+ server
56	tmux kill-server
57	
58	# or: start the new server on a new socket and migrate sessions manually
59	tmux -L new new-session -s work
60	```
61	
62	Verify with `tmux -V` (binary version) and, inside tmux, `#{version}` in a format string (server version).
63	
64	## Reload Config
65	
66	Most changes do not need a server restart.
67	
68	```bash
69	tmux source-file ~/.tmux.conf
70	```
71	
72	Or, inside tmux: `prefix + R` (shows a confirmation message after reloading).
73	
74	If a change still behaves wrong, try a new pane/window first. Only `tmux kill-server` when a terminal-capability or plugin-init issue clearly survives a reload — e.g. switching themes without leftover styling.
75	
76	## Exit vs Detach
77	
78	- `prefix + d` — detach the current client, leaving the session running
79	- `exit` — close the current shell; when the last pane exits, the session ends
80	- `prefix + :` then `kill-session` — kill the current session immediately
81	- `tmux kill-server` — kill every session and stop the server
82	
83	`detach-on-destroy off` is set, so when you kill a session tmux switches to another one instead of detaching if other sessions exist.
84	
85	## Prefix Key
86	
87	Default: `Ctrl + b`. Examples in the sibling docs assume `prefix = Ctrl + b`.
88	
89	## Plugins
90	
91	| Plugin | Purpose |
92	|--------|---------|
93	| `tmux-resurrect` | Save/restore sessions across tmux restarts |
94	| `tmux-continuum` | Automatic session saving |
95	| `tmux-floax` | Floating scratch pane (`prefix+F` toggle, `prefix+P` menu) |
96	| `tmux-fzf-url` | `prefix+u` opens fzf popup with all URLs in pane |
97	| `tmux-open` | In copy-mode: `o` opens selection, `C-o` in editor, `S` search |
98	| `catppuccin/tmux` | Status bar theme (mocha, top bar) — default |
99	| `tmux2k` | Status bar theme (onedark, bottom bar) — alternative |
100	
101	Managed by TPM; `prefix + I` to install, `prefix + U` to update.
102	
103	## Verify current config
104	
105	```bash
106	ls ~/.config/tmux/
107	tmux display-message -p '#{@theme_variant}'
108	tmux list-keys -T prefix
109	tmux show-options -s | rg 'extended-keys|extended-keys-format|default-terminal'
110	tmux show-options -g | rg 'status|focus-events'

 `./README.md`

```text
1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
11	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
12	
13	## Architecture
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart TB
17	    subgraph Bootstrap["1. Bootstrap"]
18	        BREW[Homebrew macOS]
19	        UV[uv] --> ANS[ansible]
20	        MISE[mise]
21	    end
22	
23	    subgraph Chezmoi["2. chezmoi apply"]
24	        DOT[Config files<br/>~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/]
25	        ANSDIR[~/.ansible/]
26	        BREWFILE[Brewfiles<br/>~/.config/homebrew/]
27	    end
28	
29	    subgraph Ansible["3. Ansible Playbooks"]
30	        BASE[base]
31	        ZSH[zsh]
32	        NVIM[neovim]
33	        DEVTOOLS[devtools]
34	        UVTOOLS[python_uv_tools]
35	        CARGO[rust_cargo_tools]
36	        LLMTOOLS[llm_tools]
37	    end
38	
39	    subgraph BrewBundle["4. Brew Bundle opt-in"]
40	        CASKS[GUI Apps]
41	        MAS[App Store]
42	    end
43	
44	    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible
45	    Chezmoi -.-> BrewBundle
46	    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM
47	    MISE -.->|Rust| CARGO
48	    UV -.->|Python tools| UVTOOLS
49	    UV -.->|LiteLLM| LLMTOOLS
50	    BREW -.->|casks| CASKS
51	    BREW -.->|formulae / casks| LLMTOOLS
52	```
53	
54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	```bash
57	# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
58	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
59	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
60	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
61	
62	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
63	#   chezmoi cd
64	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
65	#   exit
66	```
67	
68	This automatically:
69	
70	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
71	2. Deploys all config files
72	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
73	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled)
74	
75	### After install
76	
77	- `~/.local/bin` is auto-appended to `~/.bashrc` so `chezmoi`, `uv`, and `mise` stay reachable from bash.
78	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible `zsh` role switches your login shell to zsh automatically. Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` now.
79	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER`.
80	- Open a new shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) after install so PATH changes take effect.
81	
82	### Optional Components
83	
84	During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
85	
86	| Option | Default | Description |
87	|--------|---------|-------------|
88	| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, RTK, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
89	| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
90	| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.) |
91	| `installLlmTools` | false | Local LLM tools: Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit, models |
92	| `installAiDesktopApps` | false | macOS AI desktop apps via Homebrew Brewfile (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenCode Desktop, Antigravity, Codex Desktop on Apple Silicon; `ollama-app` also requires `installLlmTools=true`) |
93	| `installBrewApps` | false | General GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (terminals, browsers, utilities, mas; excludes AI desktop apps) |
94	| `installInputMethod` | false | Traditional Chinese input methods (McBopomofo, RIME/Squirrel on macOS; ibus-rime on Linux) |
95	| `installNetworkingTools` | false | Networking CLI tools (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, rustscan, etc.) |
96	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
97	
98	To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
99	
100	## What You Get
101	
102	### Config Files
103	
104	- `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
105	- `~/.config/git/hooks/` - Global Git hooks (pre-commit + Git LFS hooks)
106	- `~/.config/gh-dash/config.yml` - Global gh-dash config, with `diffnav` as the diff pager
107	- `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml` - Global LazyGit config, with `delta` as the custom diff pager
108	- `~/.config/bat/themes/tokyonight_night.tmTheme` - Managed Tokyo Night theme for bat
109	- `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
110	- `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
111	- `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
112	- `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
113	- `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
114	- `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config (CSI-u keybindings for `Ctrl+Number` tmux window switching, `option_as_alt` for Meta keys)
115	- `~/.config/ghostty/config` - Ghostty/cmux terminal config (`macos-option-as-alt` for tmux Meta keybindings, disabled ligatures) ([docs](docs/tools/ghostty.md))
116	- `~/.config/starship.toml` - Starship cross-shell prompt config
117	- `~/.config/direnv/direnvrc` - direnv helper functions, including `.venv`-aware Python activation
118	- `~/.config/yazi/` - Yazi file manager config (v0.3.3+ syntax, [docs](https://yazi-rs.github.io/docs/configuration/overview/))
119	  - `yazi.toml` - Main config with open rules and openers (`o`/`O`)
120	  - `keymap.toml`, `theme.toml` - Optional customization files (stubs provided)
121	- `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
122	- `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` - Global SpecStory defaults for `specstory run` across all projects
123	- `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins (resurrect, continuum, tmux-floax floating pane, tmux-fzf-url, tmux-open), vim-style copy mode with clipboard yank, capture-pane helpers (`prefix+y`/`Y`/`C-y`), a native popup menu (`prefix+Space`) with layout/resize/session management, vim-style pane nav, `Ctrl+1..9` quick window switching (CSI-u terminals), extended-keys for coding agents (including `Ctrl+/` in Neovim), sesh keybindings (`prefix+g` fzf picker, `prefix+T` television picker, `prefix+O` built-in picker, `prefix+W` window picker, `prefix+S` last), responsive Catppuccin status bar (adapts modules to terminal width for mobile), and config reload on `prefix+R` ([docs](docs/tools/tmux/README.md))
124	- `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
125	- `~/bin/sms` - Huawei router SMS reader (HiLink XML API; verification-code extraction, clipboard integration, TV channel) ([docs](docs/tools/sms.md))
126	- `~/.config/sms/config.toml.example` - Starter config for the `sms` CLI (real `config.toml` is created at runtime, never committed)
127	- `~/.config/television/cable/sms.toml` - Television channel for browsing router SMS inbox
128	- `~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml` - Sesh session manager config (named sessions with windows, wildcards, defaults) ([docs](docs/tools/sesh.md))
129	- `~/.config/television/cable/sesh.toml` - Television custom cable channel for sesh (overrides built-in with richer sources and actions)
130	- `~/.config/television/cable/lan-devices.toml` + `~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh` - Television channel for LAN device discovery with open ports, MAC/vendor, hostname, RTT; streams results incrementally via a cache file ([docs](docs/tools/tv.md))
131	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh` - Sesh keybinding (`Alt+S` for session picker), `shere`/`sroot` session helpers (supports bare command args, e.g. `shere specstory run codex`), and shell completion
132	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
133	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh` - GitHub helper with `ghget` for downloading a repo subdirectory from a tree URL
134	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/37_lazygit.zsh` - LazyGit shell alias: `lg`
135	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
136	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/29_marimo.zsh` - `marimo` zsh shell completion
137	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/26_eza.zsh` - `eza`-backed `ls`/`la`/`ll` aliases, plus `llt` for tree view with git-aware subdirectory context
138	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` - `try-cli` shell integration, with default `TRY_PATH` and graduate-friendly `TRY_PROJECTS`
139	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/94_ssh_agent.zsh` - SSH agent with Bitwarden-first fallback to persistent `ssh-agent` (auto-loads keys)
140	- `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI zsh completion
141	- `~/.ssh/config` - SSH main config skeleton (create-only: `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` + conservative `Host *` defaults)
142	- `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` - SSH global defaults stub (commented examples only)
143	- `~/.ssh/config.d/git` - SSH host entries for `github.com` and `gitlab.com` with commented multi-account/Bitwarden examples
144	- `~/.config/tmuxp/claude-sidecar.yaml` - tmuxp workspace for Claude + Sidecar
145	- `~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml` - tmuxp workspace for coding agent (nvim 75% | specstory 25%, btop tab)
146	- `~/.config/tmuxinator/coding-agent.yml` - tmuxinator workspace for coding agent (alternative to tmuxp, native sesh integration)
147	- `~/.config/tmuxinator/chezmoi.yml` - tmuxinator workspace for chezmoi session (shell + lazygit + nvim overrides, native sesh integration)
148	- `~/.config/zellij/config.kdl` - Zellij config (locked default mode for coding agent compatibility, kitty keyboard protocol)
149	- `~/.config/zellij/layouts/claude-sidecar.kdl` - Zellij layout for Claude + Sidecar
150	- `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas) plus selected CLI formulas (e.g., `tailscale`)
151	
152	SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.
153	
154	### Tools (via ansible)
155	
156	- **Base**: git, git-lfs, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
157	- **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
158	- **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
159	- **Git review stack**: gh, glab, gh-dash (via `gh` extension), diffnav, git-delta, lazygit
160	- **Markdown reader**: `glow` for terminal Markdown rendering
161	- **Shell testing**: `bats` (bats-core) — Bash test runner with TAP/JUnit output
162	- **DuckDB CLI**: `duckdb` (Homebrew on macOS, official downloads on Linux)
163	- **rclone**: cloud storage sync CLI (Homebrew on macOS, official downloads on Linux)
164	- **Ruby gem tools**: `try-cli` for ephemeral workspaces with graduate-to-project defaults, `tmuxinator` for declarative tmux session layouts (native sesh integration), plus `toolkami`
165	- **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, RTK, SpecStory, OpenChamber, td, sidecar, specify-cli
166	- **Bitwarden** (optional): Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) via npm, Desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, cask on macOS) on desktop profiles, with zsh completion and SSH agent auto-detection
167	- **LLM tools** (optional): Ollama local runtime, LiteLLM proxy, `llmfit` hardware-fit recommender, `models` TUI/CLI for model discovery and benchmarks
168	- **Input Methods** (optional): McBopomofo + RIME (Squirrel on macOS, ibus-rime on Linux)
169	- **Networking tools** (optional): nmap, arp-scan, mtr, iperf3, doggo, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, speedtest, rustscan
170	- **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
171	- **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager)
172	- **GUI Apps** (macOS): general terminals, editors, browsers, network tools, and utilities via Brewfile when `installBrewApps=true`, including developer apps like `dbeaver-community` and `superset` (Apple Silicon only); AI desktop apps via Brewfile when `installAiDesktopApps=true` (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `opencode-desktop`, `antigravity`, `codex-app` on Apple Silicon only, and `ollama-app` only when `installLlmTools=true`); Tailscale Desktop via Mac App Store `mas`, avoids pkg sudo prompt; Tailscale CLI via `brew "tailscale"` in shared Brewfile
173	
174	### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
175	- **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
176	- **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
177	- **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (ensures latest versions)
178	- **Dev tools**: bat, bats, gh, glab, diffnav, git-delta, git-graph, eza, tldr, glow, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, superfile, tmux+tpm, sesh, zellij, btop, htop, taplo, television
179	- **Alacritty**: GPU-accelerated terminal emulator (cargo install on Linux, Homebrew cask on macOS; desktop only)
180	- **Starship**: Cross-shell prompt (replaces oh-my-zsh theme)
181	- **Python tools (via uv)**: thefuck, apprise, sqlit-tui, dotenv, git-filter-repo, mlflow, tmuxp
182	- **NerdFonts**: Hack Nerd Font for terminal emulators
183	
184	## Supported Platforms
185	
186	| Platform | Package Manager | Notes |
187	|----------|-----------------|-------|
188	| macOS | Homebrew | Full support |
189	| Ubuntu Desktop | apt + snap | Full support |
190	| Ubuntu Server | apt + snap | Full support |
191	| Ubuntu Server (no root) | GitHub binaries + mise + cargo + uv | `noRoot=true`, tools installed to `~/.local/bin` |
192	| Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit OS) | apt + Linuxbrew | Full support (same as Ubuntu Server) |
193	| Raspberry Pi 4 (32-bit OS) | apt + GitHub binaries | Linuxbrew skipped; some tools without armhf builds are skipped |

195	## Manual Commands
196	
197	```bash
198	chezmoi diff          # Preview changes
199	chezmoi apply         # Apply config files
200	chezmoi cd            # Go to source directory
201	
202	# Re-run ansible manually
203	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
204	```

211	# Build and run test suite
212	just docker-test
213	
214	# Interactive devbox shell
215	just docker-run
216	
217	# Build specific profiles
218	just docker-desktop    # Ubuntu desktop profile
219	just docker-china      # China mirror profile
220	```

-- Options are automatically loaded before lazy.nvim startup
-- Default options that are always set: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/main/lua/lazyvim/config/options.lua
-- Add any additional options here

-- System clipboard integration for yank/paste
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"

-- Over SSH, route the + / * registers through OSC 52 so yanks land in the
-- LOCAL terminal's clipboard. Without this, the default provider shells out
-- to pbcopy/xclip on the REMOTE host, which is useless for pasting locally.
-- Locally (no SSH), keep LazyVim's default provider so paste also works.
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end

--- a/.config/ghostty/config
+++ b/.config/ghostty/config
@@ -8,3 +8,11 @@ macos-option-as-alt = left
 
 # Disable ligatures (code readability)
 font-features = -calt, -liga, -dlig
+
+# OSC 52 clipboard policy (pairs with tmux set-clipboard + Neovim SSH clipboard
+# override in dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua).
+# - write = allow : let inner apps (Neovim, tmux) set the system clipboard

--- a/.config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua

 -- Options are automatically loaded before lazy.nvim startup
 -- Default options that are always set: https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/blob/main/lua/lazyvim/config/options.lua
 -- Add any additional options here
+
+-- System clipboard integration for yank/paste
+vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"
+
+-- Over SSH, route the + / * registers through OSC 52 so yanks land in the
+-- LOCAL terminal's clipboard. Without this, the default provider shells out
+-- to pbcopy/xclip on the REMOTE host, which is useless for pasting locally.
+-- Locally (no SSH), keep LazyVim's default provider so paste also works.
+if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
+  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
+  vim.g.clipboard = {
+    name = "OSC 52",
+    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
+    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
+  }
+end
diff --git a/.config/tmux/common.conf b/.config/tmux/common.conf
index 9b83c405f82795cb3c90f455b1275f5698d62d38..5b722a9747f4988b5b638016c10ab59d02aa4d74 100644
--- a/.config/tmux/common.conf
+++ b/.config/tmux/common.conf
@@ -78,5 +78,15 @@
 # OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
 set -g set-clipboard on
 
+# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
+# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
+# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
+# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
+# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
+# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
+set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
+set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
+set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
+
 # Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
 set -g allow-passthrough on

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-21 01:11:05Z)**_

Done. Here's what changed and why:

**Primary fix — `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`**
Adds `vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"` and, only when `$SSH_CONNECTION` / `$SSH_TTY` is set, overrides `vim.g.clipboard` to the builtin `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52`. Local sessions keep LazyVim's default provider so `pbcopy`/`xclip` paste still works.

**tmux — `dot_config/tmux/common.conf`**
Added three `terminal-features ...:clipboard` declarations (`xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) so tmux emits OSC 52 independently of whether `tmux-256color` terminfo carries `Ms`. Kept `set -g set-clipboard on` as-is (correcting the external note's suggestion to switch to `external` — `on` is the right choice).

**Ghostty — `dot_config/ghostty/config`**
Pinned `clipboard-write = allow` / `clipboard-read = ask` explicitly so the policy is self-documenting.

**Docs**
- New "OSC 52 Clipboard" section in `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` with verification commands (`tmux info | grep -Ei 'clipboard|Ms:'`, `:checkhealth provider.clipboard`) and a terminal-support matrix.
- One-line update in `CLAUDE.md` under tmux "Key Settings for Coding Agents".
- README `Config Files` entries for `~/.config/nvim/` and `~/.config/ghostty/config` updated.

**To activate on an already-running tmux server**: `tmux kill-server` (or let it pick up naturally on next fresh attach). On the remote Neovim side, just reopen after `chezmoi apply`.

**Deferred (not done)**: `prefix + y / Y / C-y` still shell out to `pbcopy`/`xclip`, which breaks over SSH. Flagged in the plan file as a follow-up — changing them risks regressing local behaviour.

I found comprehensive information about tmux clipboard integration. Here's what the search results reveal about the topics in your query:

## OSC 52 and tmux Clipboard

OSC 52 is one of the operating system control sequences that enables clipboard management. A big advantage of this is that it works over an ssh(1) connection even if X11 forwarding is not configured.

## Remote SSH Clipboard Solutions

pbcopy and xclip approaches work great when running tmux locally, but they break down over SSH – copy operations will just sync text to the remote server's clipboard. For remote scenarios, there are 2 extra methods: Use the ANSI OSC 52 escape sequence to talk to controlling/parent terminal to manage and store text on a clipboard of a local machine, or setup a local network listener which pipes input to pbcopy or xclip, and pipe copied selected text from remote machine to a listener on the local machine through SSH remote tunneling.

## load-buffer and -w Flag

Pipe the text to be copied into tmux load-buffer instead of passing it as an argument to tmux set-buffer, thereby avoiding any shell (mis)interpretation.

## tmux set-clipboard Option

tmux supports this through the set-clipboard option. set-clipboard does not work when you have a remote tmux session nested in a local one, and it only works in those terminals which supports OSC 52 escape sequence handling.

The results include practical implementation details and configuration examples for clipboard integration across local and remote tmux sessions.

Based on the search results, here's information about tmux, `set-buffer -w`, OSC 52, clipboard integration, and SSH best practices:

## OSC 52 and Clipboard Integration

OSC 52 is an operating system control sequence that enables clipboard synchronization. A key advantage is that it works over an ssh(1) connection even if X11 forwarding is not configured.

## set-clipboard Option

For set-clipboard to work, the set-clipboard option must be set to on or external. The difference is that "on" makes tmux set the clipboard for the outside terminal and allows applications inside tmux to set tmux's clipboard, while "external" only makes tmux set the clipboard and forbids applications inside from doing so.

## Security Considerations

With set-clipboard set to on, great care must be taken with untrusted commands run inside tmux. This is an important best practice consideration for SSH sessions.

## SSH Best Practices

For SSH sessions, ensure your terminal supports OSC 52 escape sequences by setting: `set-option -g allow-passthrough on` and `set-option -g terminal-features 'xterm*:clipboard'`

## Terminal Configuration

For tmux 3.2 or later, add: `set -as terminal-features ',rxvt-unicode-256color:clipboard'` (changing the terminal name as appropriate for your TERM)

# Clipboard & OSC 52

This doc explains how clipboard sync is wired across this dotfiles setup, with a focus on **OSC 52** — the escape sequence that lets a remote SSH session put text on your **local** machine's clipboard.

## TL;DR

| You are… | Yank in Neovim goes to… | Capture pane (`prefix+y/Y/C-y`) goes to… |
|----------|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| Local (macOS or Linux desktop) | system clipboard (default provider: `pbcopy` / `wl-copy` / `xclip`) | same, via `tmux load-buffer -w -` which emits OSC 52 *and* sets tmux's paste buffer |
| SSH (remote box, with or without tmux) | **local** machine's clipboard (via OSC 52) | **local** machine's clipboard (via tmux → OSC 52) |

No extra tools, no X forwarding, no socat listener needed. The only hard requirement is a terminal emulator on your **local** machine that supports OSC 52 (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, Kitty, WezTerm — all do).

## What is OSC 52?

`OSC 52` is an ANSI escape sequence:

\```
ESC ] 52 ; c ; <base64-of-data> BEL
\```

Any program that can write to a terminal can emit this sequence; the terminal emulator on the other end decodes the base64 and writes it to the system clipboard. The crucial property: **escape sequences travel up the TTY back to the client terminal**, so this works transparently over SSH, mosh, and nested `tmux ssh` chains — no display server, no socket forwarding.

Tradeoffs:

- **Write** is ubiquitous. Most modern terminals allow it by default or with a simple opt-in.
- **Read** (paste from local clipboard back into remote apps) is much less supported — many terminals refuse for obvious security reasons (a malicious server could exfiltrate your clipboard). Ghostty prompts; Alacritty flat-out ignores it.
- A terminal multiplexer (tmux, screen, zellij) sits between the inner app and the outer terminal. It must be configured to either **emit** OSC 52 to its host terminal or **pass through** OSC 52 from inner apps.

Reference: [tmux Clipboard wiki](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Clipboard), [XTerm control sequences (OSC)](https://www.invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html).

## How this repo wires it up

Four layers cooperate. Removing any one silently breaks remote-clipboard sync.

### 1. Terminal emulator (outer, on your local machine)

Must accept OSC 52 writes from whatever is running inside it.

**Ghostty / cmux** — [`dot_config/ghostty/config`](../../dot_config/ghostty/config):

\```conf
clipboard-write = allow   # let inner apps set the system clipboard
clipboard-read  = ask     # prompt before reads (safer default)
\```

Both match current Ghostty defaults but are pinned explicitly so policy drifts from upstream don't silently break (or weaken) this chain.

**Alacritty** — native support, no config needed. Paste from OSC 52 not supported.

**iTerm2 / Kitty / WezTerm** — native support. iTerm2 requires `Preferences → General → Selection → Applications in terminal may access clipboard` for reads.

### 2. Multiplexer — tmux

[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf):

\```tmux
set -g set-clipboard on

set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"

set -g allow-passthrough on
\```

- **`set-clipboard on`** — tmux both re-emits OSC 52 to the outer terminal when its own copy-mode yanks, and passes OSC 52 from inner apps (Neovim, less, etc.) through. `external` would only pass through; `on` is a strict superset and simpler.
- **`terminal-features …:clipboard`** — tells tmux the outer terminal supports OSC 52 without needing a terminfo `Ms` capability. Many distros ship a `tmux-256color` entry that lacks `Ms`, so declaring the feature directly avoids surprises when `chezmoi apply` is run on a fresh box.
- **`allow-passthrough on`** — lets terminal-image protocols (sixel, kitty graphics) work; also covers OSC passthrough for nested multiplexers.

**Capture-pane helpers** — [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf) — use the tmux-native idiom rather than shelling out:

\```tmux
bind y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p   | tmux load-buffer -w -"
bind Y   run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w -"
bind C-y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux … | tmux load-buffer -w -"
\```

`load-buffer -w -` reads stdin into tmux's paste buffer *and* (because of `-w`) forwards to the system clipboard via OSC 52. Previously these bindings used a `pbcopy | xclip | xsel` fallback chain that only worked locally — over SSH they copied to the **remote** machine's clipboard, which is useless. The tmux-native form works identically in both places.

`set-buffer -w …` offers the same `-w` flag but takes data as an argument, which introduces shell-quoting landmines on multi-line pane content; `load-buffer -w -` reads stdin and sidesteps that.

### 3. Editor — Neovim

[`dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`](../../dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua):

\```lua
vim.opt.clipboard = "unnamedplus"

if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy  = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"),  ["*"] = osc52.copy("*")  },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end
\```

- Locally, LazyVim's default provider is used (`pbcopy`/`xclip`/`wl-copy` — with working paste).
- Over SSH, Neovim's built-in `vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` (shipping since Neovim 0.10) emits OSC 52 directly, bypassing any `pbcopy` binary on the remote host.
- The check is `SSH_CONNECTION or SSH_TTY` — either is set by `sshd` for an interactive session.

Why conditional rather than always-on OSC 52? OSC 52 paste is unreliable (see the terminal table above). Keeping the local provider for local sessions preserves Neovim's paste behaviour; the override only activates when `pbcopy` on the remote is clearly the wrong answer.

### 4. Shell CLI — `x` (cross-platform clipboard wrapper)

[`bin/executable_x`](../../bin/executable_x) (deployed to `~/.local/bin/x`) is a Bash wrapper with three subcommands:

\```bash
printf "hello" | x copy        # copy stdin to clipboard
x copy path/to/file            # copy file contents
x paste                        # print clipboard to stdout
x open https://example.com     # open URL/file in default app
\```

Its copy backend tries, in order: `clip.exe` (WSL) → `pbcopy` (macOS) → `wl-copy` (Wayland) → `xclip` → `xsel` → **OSC 52 fallback** writing directly to `/dev/tty`. This means `x copy` Just Works on macOS, Linux desktop, Linux SSH server, WSL, and anything else that can reach a terminal — you never have to think about which backend is available.

The OSC 52 fallback in `x` is also wrapped for tmux:

\```bash
if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
  printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
else
  printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
fi
\```

The `DCS tmux; ... ST` wrapper is tmux's passthrough escape — it tells tmux "hand this sequence to the outer terminal as-is", needed because tmux otherwise intercepts OSC 52.

## Verifying the chain works

On the remote box where Neovim yank is misbehaving, run:

\```bash
# tmux: does it believe the terminal can accept OSC 52?
tmux info | grep -Ei 'clipboard|Ms:'
# expect: clipboard: true  and an Ms entry that is NOT [missing]

# shell: can x copy reach the clipboard?
printf "hello from %s" "$(hostname)" | x copy
# then Cmd+V / Ctrl+V into a local app → should paste "hello from <remote-host>"

# Neovim: which provider is active?
nvim -c ':checkhealth provider.clipboard' -c ':only'
# expect: OSC 52 under SSH, native under local
\```

If `tmux info` shows `clipboard: false` after editing `common.conf`, remember a running tmux server **keeps its old capability table** — `tmux kill-server` (losing sessions; `tmux-resurrect` can restore them) and re-attach.

## Common failure modes

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|-------------|-----|
| Yank works outside tmux but vanishes inside tmux (remote) | `set-clipboard off` or server running pre-edit binary | `tmux show -g set-clipboard`; `tmux kill-server` |
| `tmux info` shows `Ms: [missing]` | tmux's TERM entry lacks `Ms` *and* no `terminal-features …:clipboard` declared | already handled by [`common.conf`](../../dot_config/tmux/common.conf); on an unusual outer `$TERM`, add another `set -as terminal-features` line |
| Ghostty asks about clipboard every yank | `clipboard-read = ask`; Ghostty interprets some writes as reads when apps immediately re-fetch | switch to `clipboard-read = allow` if you trust everything inside your sessions |
| Neovim yank works, but `"*p` does nothing over SSH | paste over OSC 52 not supported by outer terminal | expected — use mouse middle-click or re-type; don't fight it |
| `prefix+y` still copies to remote clipboard | shim binary `tmux` resolves to an old pre-`load-buffer -w` version | `tmux -V` must be ≥ 3.3 for `load-buffer -w`; this repo enforces ≥ 3.3 via ansible `devtools` role |
| Nested tmux (`tmux inside ssh inside tmux`) | inner tmux eats OSC 52 | inner tmux needs `set -g allow-passthrough on`; already on in this config. Double-nested cases may require `Ptmux;…` wrapping |

## Design notes / non-defaults

- **tmux `set-clipboard`** is `on`, not `external`. `external` disables tmux's own OSC 52 emission from copy-mode; `on` is a superset and keeps `prefix+[` → `y` working.
- **Neovim OSC 52 provider** is gated on `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_TTY` rather than always-on, specifically so local paste (`"+p`) continues to work. If you primarily work over SSH and don't mind the paste tradeoff, the `if …` block can be removed.
- **`x` CLI ordering** prefers local backends (`pbcopy`, `wl-copy`, etc.) over OSC 52. This is intentional: when `pbcopy` is available, it's faster, doesn't touch the TTY, and works for very large payloads (OSC 52 payloads are size-limited by the terminal — iTerm2 caps at 1 MB, many others at 64-256 KB).

- [`bin/executable_x`](../../bin/executable_x) — the `x` wrapper source
